messages:
olivia: quick update — ran a rapid int6 quant sweep for orion-13b on the dev fleet (small slices). uploading a short digest of cost vs quality.
ben: awesome, can you post the delta numbers? unit econ is what product is asking for this week.
olivia: yes — rough headline: token-cost down ~42%, p50 latency +8ms, p95 +28ms. quality: short Q/A NLG BLEU ~ -0.3, long-form ROUGE / factuality slices show 0.6–1.2 pts drop depending on prompt style.
sasha: do you have per-slice deltas? especially recall slices from docs-heavy prompts.
olivia: pasted sample slices below (trimmed):
```
slice: docs-retrieval-long 
- baseline (fp16): rouge-L=38.4, latency p95=420ms, cost=1.00x
- int6 quant: rouge-L=37.1 (-1.3), latency p95=448ms (+28), cost=0.58x

slice: chat-short 
- baseline: bleu=29.1, p95=240ms, cost=1.00x
- int6: bleu=28.9 (-0.2), p95=250ms (+10), cost=0.58x
```

ben: thanks — that docs slice delta is non-trivial. any specific failure modes? hallucination uptick? maya_p: product lead here — we need to quantify user impact. small BLEU delta ok, but hallucination regressions are dealbreakers.
olivia: flagged hallucination on ~3% of docs samples (vs 1.2% baseline). mainly when prompts rely on verbatim long context + aggressive summarization.
sasha: can we mitigate with a 2-tier routing fallback? use int6 by default, route docs-retrieval-long to fp16 or int8 when prompt contains >2k tokens or has retrieval traces.en: that's what routing is for. we should compute the break-even: extra cost for fallback vs user-visible quality metric.
olivia: quick math: fallback to fp16 for 10% of traffic (the docs-like slice) adds ~4.2% cost overall while recovering ~1.3 pts rouge-L on that slice.
maya_p: from GTN/product POV — 4.2% cost to recover a 1.3 ROUGE on a critical slice probably acceptable if docs use-case maps to paid users. need a recommendation for rollout flags.
olivia: propose config:
- pilot 5% global traffic int6 default.
- route identified docs-retrieval-long (prompt classifier) to fp16.
- enable roll-forward to 20% if prod metrics (ROUGE proxy, hallucination rate) stable after 48h.

sasha: +1 on classifier routing. can we implement a lightweight prompt heuristic in the router: token_count>1800 || contains("source:") || retrieval=true -> route to fp16.
ben: add a canary metric: hallucination_rate (automated eval) and avg_token_cost. break glass if hallucination_rate > baseline+1.5%.
eval-bot: automated slice check ran:
summary: pilot 5% int6 -> hallucination +0.6% overall, docs slice +1.3%; unit cost reduced 38% on pilot traffic.
thresholds: trigger if overall hallucination > +1.0% within 24h.
maya_p: product ok with pilot 5% and classifier routing. need a short note for GTN with the ROI numbers and rollback thresholds.en: I'll draft the handoff doc. action items:
- olivia: push router heuristic + canary flags (ETA 6h)
- sasha: add automated eval slice to monitoring (eta 12h)
- ben: draft GTN note + cost table (eta EOD)
- maya_p: align on customer impact criteria (eta EOD)

olivia: started a PR for router rule: https://github.com/redwood/rex/pull/4823 : contains the token_count heuristic and a toggle `route_docs_to_fp16`.
ben: nice. once merged I'll wire the rollout in console.
sasha: remember to include observability: per-route cost, p95 latency, hallucination proxy (qa-check count) and rouge-L on sampled logs.
maya_p: thanks team. if pilot looks good we'll expand to 25% next week. :rocket:
olivia: will post a short followup after first 24h with eval-bot summary. :thumbsup:
